text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40

Robusta September coffee futures' may advance above $1,600 but this would probably be shortlived and the market is more likely to retreat and re-test key support below $1,500, technical analysts said on Monday.
Traders called the market to open unchanged.
New York arabica coffee futures finished broadly lower in dull trading Friday, pressured by light commission house selling, dealers said.
Benchmark September arabicas ended down 4.10 cents at 176.30 cents a lb after ranging from 182.00 to 175.50.
Technically, traders said September support was seen near 174.25 cents. They continued to peg resistance at 184.50 cents -- a double top on the charts -- followed by 192.00 to 193.00 cents.
In London, the September contract hit an intraday high of $1,617 but finished just below the $1,600 level -- the fifth straight day that the market had closed below that level.
Technically, the immediate resistance is pegged at $1,612, followed by just below $1,650 and then $1,750, said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst.
"But it's more likely to retreat and re-test support at just below $1,500, with the likely target seen at $1,455," she said.
Other traders said the LIFFE contract was likely to continue its consolidation phase without any clear immediate direction.
The September contract hit a six-month low of $1,477 last week on the back of fund long liquidation.
The 14-day relative strength of oversold/overbought indicator stood at 38 percent on Friday, just above the 30-percent value oversold condition.
July 31 is the last day for trading and tender day for the spot July contract. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
